threats.title: Eight eMudhra intermediate CA private keys compromised
threats.headline: Flawed key generation exposed eight eMudhra intermediate CA keys, risking site impersonation for non-browser TLS clients
threats.summary: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were incorrectly generated and can be recovered from the certificates. An attacker with any of these keys could impersonate any website or service, mainly against clients that do not enforce Certificate Transparency or consume revocation information. Major browsers block the intermediates, the CA revoked them, and many trust stores and developer packages have shipped updates.

affects.name: macOS built-in curl, git, python3, perl, ruby and openssl

actions: Update browsers, operating systems and language runtimes to the patched versions.
Upgrade bundled trust stores in your Python, Node.js, Go and Rust toolchains.
Check that TLS clients outside the browser no longer trust the compromised intermediates.
On macOS, remember that built-in command-line tools still use an outdated certificate file.
who: TLS clients that do not enforce Certificate Transparency
Developers relying on bundled trust stores
threats.quote: An attacker with the private key of any of the compromised intermediate CAs could impersonate any website or service.

threats.title: uv bundled CA store trusts compromised emSign root
threats.headline: uv before 0.13.4 accepts certificates from compromised eMudhra intermediates, enabling MITM attacks on its TLS connections
threats.summary: uv verifies TLS against a vendored webpki-root-certs bundle that included the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root before version 0.13.4. Eight eMudhra intermediates chaining to that root have compromised private keys, so an attacker holding one could issue certificates uv accepts for any hostname and mount MITM attacks. uv 0.13.4 removes the root from its bundle.
actions: Upgrade uv to 0.13.4 or later.
Rebuild environments and CI images that pin an older uv.
who: CI pipelines that install packages with uv
threats.quote: An attacker with one of the compromised keys can issue certificates that uv accepts for any hostname, and can be used to issue certificates to enable MITM attacks.

threats.title: certifi bundle includes root with compromised intermediates
threats.headline: certifi before 2026.10.19 trusts a root over compromised eMudhra intermediates, exposing requests, urllib3 and pip
threats.summary: Certifi bundled the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root, to which eight eMudhra intermediates with compromised private keys chain. An attacker with one key can issue valid-looking certificates for any hostname and, if on-path, intercept or modify TLS traffic from clients such as requests, urllib3 and pip. Certifi 2026.10.19 removes the affected roots and keeps the unaffected emSign roots.
actions: Upgrade certifi to 2026.10.19 or later.
Rebuild container images that vendor certifi.
who: Python apps using requests, urllib3 or pip
Users of the Python.org macOS installer
threats.quote: If the attacker is also on-path, they can intercept or modify TLS traffic from clients that trust the certifi bundle.

threats.title: MCP TypeScript SDK servers crashable by one request
threats.headline: A single unauthenticated HTTP request can exhaust memory and crash MCP TypeScript SDK servers
threats.summary: Affected MCP TypeScript SDK servers did not limit how many array elements and object keys they validated in one request. One request under the default 4 MiB size limit could exhaust memory and abort the process, with no credentials needed. Patched versions add a maxToolInputElements option that is off by default, so builders must turn it on and also lower the request size limit.
actions: Upgrade the SDK and set maxToolInputElements just above your largest expected tool input.
Lower the request body size limit to what your tools need.
If you cannot upgrade, cap request size at the transport or a reverse proxy.
who: MCP servers reachable over HTTP by untrusted clients
McpServer tools that accept arrays or records
threats.quote: In affected versions, servers put no limit on how many array elements and object keys they validated in one request.

threats.title: MCP TypeScript SDK experimental tasks lacked session isolation
threats.headline: MCP SDK servers sharing a task store let clients list, read and cancel other sessions' tasks
threats.summary: The deprecated experimental tasks feature in the MCP TypeScript SDK did not check which session created a task. Clients sharing one InMemoryTaskStore could list, read and cancel each other's tasks. Version 1.32.0 ties each task to the session that created it.
actions: Stop using the deprecated experimental tasks feature.
Upgrade to the fixed SDK version if your HTTP server passes a task store.
If you cannot upgrade, remove the task store or use one per session.
who: HTTP MCP servers that pass taskStore to McpServer or Server
threats.quote: Clients sharing one InMemoryTaskStore could list, read and cancel each other's tasks.

threats.title: rustls-webpki may accept distrusted emSign intermediates
threats.headline: rustls-webpki could accept certificate paths through emSign intermediates whose private keys are now well known
threats.summary: Affected rustls-webpki versions may accept certificate paths containing distrusted emSign intermediate public keys when the configured trust anchors allow such paths. The private keys for these intermediates are now well known. Versions 0.103.16 and 0.104.0-alpha.8 reject paths containing these public keys.
actions: Upgrade rustls-webpki to a fixed version.
Rebuild and redeploy Rust binaries that link it.
who: Rust apps and tools that verify TLS with rustls-webpki
threats.quote: The private keys corresponding to these intermediates are now well known.

threats.title: MCP TypeScript SDK bearer auth skipped audience checks
threats.headline: MCP servers using SDK bearer authentication accepted tokens issued for other services by shared authorization servers
threats.summary: The MCP TypeScript SDK's server-side bearer authentication had no way to check that a token was issued for your server. Where one authorization server issues tokens for several services, a valid token for another service was also accepted. Patched versions add an expectedResource setting that is off by default and must be enabled along with returning the token audience.
actions: Upgrade and enable the expectedResource setting with your server's audience.
Return the token audience from your access token verifier.
Until you upgrade, reject tokens whose audience does not include your server.
who: MCP servers using requireBearerAuth() or verifyBearerToken()
Deployments whose authorization server issues tokens for several services
threats.quote: Where one authorization server issues tokens for several services, a valid token for another service was also accepted by your MCP server.

threats.title: MCP TypeScript client SDK leaked secrets on cross-origin redirects
threats.headline: MCP SDK clients followed redirects to any origin, re-sending API keys, session IDs and OAuth secrets
threats.summary: The MCP TypeScript SDK's HTTP client transports and OAuth requests followed redirects to any origin. A redirect could send custom headers and the mcp-session-id header to another origin, and on a 307 or 308 also the request body, including refresh_token and client_secret. Patched versions follow redirects only within the same origin, and not at all in browsers.
actions: Upgrade the client SDK and keep the new same-origin redirect behaviour.
Configure final URLs instead of relying on cross-origin redirects.
Rotate API keys and client secrets and revoke tokens if a redirect may have reached an untrusted host.
who: Apps using the SDK's OAuth client functions
threats.quote: In affected versions, the SDK's HTTP client transports and OAuth requests followed redirects to any origin.

threats.title: vLLM penalty handler denial of service
threats.headline: Remote manipulation of vLLM's penalty handler can cause denial of service, with a public exploit
threats.summary: A flaw in vLLM affects the get_token_bin_counts_and_mask function in the Penalty Handler component. A remote attacker can manipulate it to cause denial of service, and an exploit has been released to the public. The advisory lists vLLM 0.32.0 as fixed.
actions: Upgrade vLLM to 0.32.0 or later.
Limit who can send requests to your vLLM servers until upgraded.
threats.quote: The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks.
